claims.text: The low-field magnetocaloric response of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films is primarily governed by interfacial heat dissipation.
The hysteresis of these films during low-field cooling cycles is primarily governed by interfacial heat dissipation.
Increasing substrate thermal conductivity improves heat flow across or near the film-substrate interface.
Improved interfacial heat flow sharpens the magnetostructural transition.
Improved interfacial heat flow reduces hysteresis relative to films on standard substrates.
The controlled intervention is to fabricate otherwise identical films on substrates spanning high to low thermal conductivity.
Cycle frequencies in the proposed regime are limited by interfacial heat-transfer rates.
Changes in substrate thermal transport alter local temperature gradients at the film-substrate interface.
Interfacial temperature gradients modulate coupling between magnetic and structural transitions.
A high-thermal-conductivity substrate dissipates heat faster and reduces thermal lag during magnetic-field cycling.
Reduced thermal lag makes the magnetostructural phase transition more prompt and reversible.
A more prompt and reversible magnetostructural transition narrows the magnetic hysteresis loop.
A more prompt and reversible magnetostructural transition enhances the magnetocaloric effect.
Under identical low-field cooling cycles, films on high-thermal-conductivity substrates will have narrower hysteresis loops than the baseline films.
Under identical low-field cooling cycles, films on high-thermal-conductivity substrates will exhibit a larger magnetocaloric effect than the baseline films.
The predicted behavior applies where interfacial heat-transfer limitations are significant in nanoscale films or nanoribbons.
Results from the nanoscale system may not extrapolate directly to bulk samples or high-field conditions.
Microstructural variations, interfacial stress, and processing-induced defects may affect the magnitude of hysteresis reduction and magnetocaloric enhancement.
